title: Design System: Danish Ahmed N F — Portfolio

hero.purpose: Route console headline only, one instance per page.

section-title.purpose: One per station/section, set beside its station node.

station-title.purpose: Individual entries within a section: a project, a role, a degree.

readout.purpose: Every non-prose data token: tags, dates, stats, the console route input, nav micro-labels. Always Overpass Mono.

motion.name: signal-scroll
motion.purpose: Binds the traveling signal dot's position on the spine to overall scroll progress — the page's one authored through-line motion.

motion.name: spine-draw
motion.purpose: Per-section spine segment draws in as its station enters view.

motion.name: station-entrance
motion.purpose: Section content entrance — reads as emerging from the line, distinct from the ledger system's translateY reveal. Respects prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: signal-glow-pulse
motion.purpose: Ambient pulse on the hero's 'in service' status dot and the traveling signal — the only elements permitted the Glow-Is-Lit treatment.

components.name: Station Node (simple)
components.description: The circle marking a section's position on the spine. Rail-bordered at rest; glows Signal Blue when its section is the one currently nearest the traveling signal.
components.css: .ds-station{ width:18px; height:18px; border-radius:50%; background:#0B0E14; border:2px solid #232B3A; transition:border-color .3s ease, box-shadow .3s ease; } .ds-station.is-active{ border-color:#3FA7FF; box-shadow:0 0 12px 2px rgba(63,167,255,0.55); }

components.name: Interchange Ring (project station)
components.description: A project's station ring: a conic-gradient wedge per skill line its real tags touch. A single-line project renders as one solid color, never a gradient.
components.css: .ds-interchange{ width:26px; height:26px; border-radius:50%; background:var(--seg); border:2px solid #0B0E14; outline:1px solid #232B3A; }

components.name: Signal Dot
components.description: The single traveling marker riding the spine, position bound to scroll progress. The page's signature motion element.
components.css: .ds-signal{ width:10px; height:10px; border-radius:50%; background:#3FA7FF; box-shadow:0 0 10px 3px rgba(63,167,255,0.65), 0 0 24px 8px rgba(63,167,255,0.25); }

components.name: Line Chip
components.description: Hero console control representing one of the four skill lines; square, colored border and text in that line's color.
components.css: .ds-line-chip{ font-family:'Overpass Mono',monospace; font-size:12px; letter-spacing:0.06em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--line); background:transparent; border:1px solid var(--line); padding:10px 16px; border-radius:0; cursor:pointer; transition:background .25s ease, color .25s ease; } .ds-line-chip:hover, .ds-line-chip:focus-visible{ background:var(--line); color:#0B0E14; }

components.name: Readout Tag
components.description: Tech-stack tag list under a project title. Square, mono, Steel Dim.

components.name: Station Row (project)
components.description: The dominant repeating unit: an interchange ring beside a project title, description, tags, and live link.

components.name: Route Console Input
components.css: .ds-console{ background:#10141C; border:1px solid #232B3A; padding:14px 18px; font-family:'Overpass Mono',monospace; font-size:13px; color:#7C8798; } .ds-console:focus-within{ border-color:#3FA7FF; }

narrative.overview:
The site is staged as a transit/circuit schematic: a signal-lit spine runs the length of the page, and every section is a station on it. Each of the four real skill categories (Programming, Web & Backend, Data & ML, Databases & Tools) is a named, colored line; projects are interchange stations — their station ring is a conic-gradient wedge of every line whose tech actually appears in that project's real tag list, so "breadth across full-stack and data/ML" (the product's core positioning claim) is drawn as literal infrastructure instead of asserted in a sentence. The hero is a route console the visitor operates — pick a destination, the signal travels the spine to it as the page scrolls. Nothing here is decorative cartography: every line a project touches, every interchange size, is derived from that project's real stack.

This replaced the Passbook ledger direction. Where the Passbook proved verified data, the Data Line proves versatility — the other half of the product's positioning — through dev/data-culture's own diagram language (DAGs, schematics) fused with transit-map convention.
keyCharacteristics: One continuous schematic spine carries a station marker per section; project stations get a multi-color interchange ring sized to how many lines actually converge there.
A single traveling signal dot rides the spine, position bound to scroll progress — the one authored through-line motion.
One typeface family (Overpass) does every display and body job; Overpass Mono is reserved for readouts only.
Circles are reserved exclusively for stations — nothing else is ever round.
Glow is reserved for things genuinely lit in the source material — never a decorative halo on resting content.

rules.name: The Truth-Mapped Line Rule
rules.body: A line color may only appear next to content that genuinely belongs to that skill category. Interchange-ring segments are generated from a project's real work-tags, never hand-picked for balance or color variety.

rules.name: The Glow-Is-Lit Rule
rules.body: Glow is reserved for things actually lit in the schematic world: the traveling signal dot, the active line, live/status indicators. It never appears on cards, text, or resting UI as generic polish.

rules.name: One Signage Face Rule
rules.body: Overpass carries every heading and every prose sentence; Overpass Mono carries every non-prose data token. No third typeface is introduced for personality.

rules.name: The Circle-Is-A-Station Rule
rules.body: A circle means this is a stop on the line. If a circle appears anywhere that isn't a station node or the signal dot, the shape language has broken.

rules.name: Line-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Depth and hierarchy come from line weight, color, and glow-when-lit — never from a drop shadow. A schematic doesn't cast shadows; it lights up.

dos: Do derive every interchange ring from the entry's real tags — the Truth-Mapped Line Rule.
Do keep glow reserved for genuinely lit elements — the Glow-Is-Lit Rule.
Do keep circles exclusive to stations — the Circle-Is-A-Station Rule.
Do run Overpass across every heading and body role, Overpass Mono across every data token — One Signage Face Rule.
Do keep the spine present and structurally identical on every section.
donts: Don't hand-pick interchange-ring colors for visual balance — they are computed from real tags only.
Don't add a drop shadow anywhere; depth is line weight and glow only.
Don't round a corner on anything that isn't a station or the signal dot.
Don't let the console's destination buttons be decorative — every one must actually navigate.
